key_insight: Attack-policy selection and optimisation can substantially change measured monitor evasion rates, making basic attack evaluations falsely reassuring.
engineering_relevance: Monitor assessments should test multiple attack methods and optimisation levels, while justifying how generated attacks represent dangerous deployment behaviour.
method: Evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor using attack-generated transcripts.
Vary attack-generation methods and optimisation levels.
Develop attacks against proxy monitors, then test transfer to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor.
evidence_signal: False negative rates ranged from 0.5% to 20.8% across reinforcement-learning optimisation levels and from 6.4% to 23.0% across methods at their best observed optimisation levels.
watch_item: Attack transcripts can contain artefacts that influence monitor judgements; their relevance or conservativeness for deployment remains unproven.
paper_title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
